name: Union Pacific
headline: A railroad network across 23 western states that nobody could build again.
what_it_does: Union Pacific runs a 32,889-route-mile freight railroad across 23 western states and serves all six major Mexico gateways. It hauled $23.2 billion of freight in 2025, including grain, fertilizer, industrial goods and consumer goods. Its only major rail rival in the West is BNSF.
why_it_passed: No one can lay a second 32,889-mile network into the ports, gateways and plants UNP reaches, and the rail rivals in its territory in 2025 are the same as in 2009.
Its operating ratio (operating costs as a share of revenue, lower is better) improved from 67.8% in 2012 to under 60%, and it has raised prices through inflation.
The analysis found management honest and able, and found no adverse integrity facts.
The economics can be pictured ten years out because they follow carloads times price per car.
why_not_now: The analysis values the shares at $120.64 to $162.31 against a price of $278.34, which is 1.7 times the top of the range. A buyer at that price would expect only about 2.6% to 4.5% a year, below a 30-year US Treasury bond (5.60%).
watch: It is merging with Norfolk Southern, which would add about $20 billion of new borrowing and Norfolk Southern's $15.5 billion of net debt; buybacks are paused for the deal.
Over 2016 to 2025 it paid out about $70 billion in dividends and buybacks, about $19 billion more than the cash it earned after capital spending.
Its buyback authorizations name a number of shares, never a price limit, so shares were bought above their value.
